source_review.notes: Checked 15 unique authoritative references covering Apache Avro 1.12.0 schema, resolution, encodings, containers and canonical form; current Protocol Buffers encoding, proto3, Editions, presence, best-practice, ProtoJSON and runtime guarantees; current Confluent compatibility, SerDes and contract guidance; and RFC 8949 as a comparison format.

evidence: Reviewed boundary tuple M, writer/reader schemas, encoder/resolver, compatibility relation B, version history H, payload encode/decode/resolve functions, Protobuf tag equation, varint, ZigZag, presence predicate, and unknown-field notation.
Checked directionality and quantification for backward, forward, full, pairwise, and transitive compatibility.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Schema, wire, runtime, domain, and operational variables are introduced separately and retain consistent meanings.

evidence: Executed schema-wire-audit with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced Protobuf bytes 089601120378797a, field 1/wire type 0/value 150, exact unknown raw-field preservation, Avro -1 encoding 01, Avro 64 encoding 8001, and signed round trips for -64, -1, 0, 1, and 64.
Manually recomputed tag values 8 and 18, base-128 varint 150 as 0x96 0x01, the three-byte length prefix, and ZigZag mappings -1 to 1 and 64 to 128.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite byte calculations match the chapter and are explicitly not presented as complete format implementations or performance evidence.

evidence: Re-derived encode under writer schema followed by exact-writer decode and writer-to-reader resolution.
Re-derived tag t=(field_number << 3)|wire_type and both branches of signed ZigZag mapping.
Checked that transitive backward compatibility quantifies B(S_i,S_n) over every governed historical writer while the forward direction reverses relation arguments.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The compatibility relation is intentionally contract-relative rather than claiming a universal property of schema text alone.

evidence: Reviewed missing writer schema, unknown/unauthorized registry ID, fingerprint collision, deleted registry history, stale cache, outage, rollback, mixed compiler/runtime versions, and generated-code skew.

Reviewed Avro missing/default fields, aliases, name reuse, reordered unions, every branch, unknown enum symbols, decimal precision/scale, temporal units, object-container split markers, single-object fingerprints, and codec expansion.

Reviewed Protobuf reused/reserved tags, varint truncation/overflow, length overrun, field reordering/repetition, implicit versus explicit presence, unknown-field loss through JSON/copies, enum additions, JSON names, unstable bytes, recursion, strings, collections, and messages near operational limits.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Wire, history, domain, implementation, registry, framing, allocation, and recovery boundaries all have explicit tests or controls.

evidence: Traced schema binding, field identity, resolution, presence, unknown preservation, domain meaning, governed history, and resource safety through the fourteen-step mechanism.
Verified examples never reuse a deployed Protobuf number or Avro identity for changed meaning and route grain, unit, scale, and identity changes to explicit migration.
Checked the old-reader round-trip requirement as a path property rather than assuming every runtime or JSON conversion preserves unknowns.
invariant_checking.notes: Registry acceptance is consistently treated as one gate rather than the source of every invariant.

evidence: Reviewed the three-schema constructive counterexample to adjacent-only compatibility and its dependence on direction and domain field-identity rules.
Confirmed that acceptance of adjacent S1/S2 and S2/S3 pairs cannot establish the direct S1/S3 relation when a removed identity is semantically reused.
Checked the stated conclusion: transitive format checks reduce structural gaps but still do not prove domain compatibility.
proof_review.notes: The proof separates the general non-transitivity warning from product-specific compatibility algorithms.

evidence: Confirmed the adjacent-compatibility construction is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
Audited uses of exact, durable, required, valid, safe, preserve, deterministic, canonical, compatible, and prove for stated format/profile/domain conditions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No parse success, registry result, wire-type match, fingerprint, default, or deterministic mode is promoted to unconditional semantic proof.

evidence: Confirmed schema-wire-audit is labeled a synthetic finite model and not a full Avro or Protobuf implementation.
Reviewed size, speed, ecosystem, generated/generic API, compression, and registry trade-offs as workload- and implementation-dependent.
Confirmed no production reliability, security certification, universal language behavior, performance benchmark, or external-review claim.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Current tool and product behavior is attributed to primary documentation and requires deployed-version verification.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed domain schema, writer/reader resolution, Avro names/defaults/unions/logical types/envelopes, Protobuf tags/varints/lengths/unknowns/presence/enums/JSON, compatibility direction, registries, toolchains, migrations, and observation as one layered model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed lineage ownership, exact schema binding, tag/name retirement, registry scope and recovery, populated mixed-version matrices, old intermediaries, generated/runtime pinning, bounded parsing, explicit migrations, reconciliation, and telemetry. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from domain contract through both wire mechanisms to compatibility operations; ten examples and five complete answers cover default provenance, identity retirement, byte tracing, heterogeneous gateways, archives, and incompatible numeric migration.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, Apache, Google, Confluent, data-practitioner, security, performance, or production-interoperability review is claimed.
